ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all shareholders, UBOs, legal representatives, and prospective officers against TRACFIN domestic reporting criteria, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC's SDN List, and recognized international PEP databases (e.g., World-Check, LexisNexis, Dow Jones). The protocol requires two-level adverse-media review, source-of-funds verification, and negative news validation for each UBO before engagement. Results must be documented and retained under the Code monétaire et financier Article L.561-36 for five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet des Entreprises and INPI Data (data.inpi.fr) for National Register of Enterprises (RNE) and RCS name conflict screening
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may be selected in any language, but all legal registration documents must be in French under Article L.122-1 of the Consumer Code and French commercial usage. Non-Latin scripts, ideograms, or Cyrillic names must be transliterated into Latin characters for the RCS entry. The name may not include misleading terms, terms implying a regulated activity, or terms that are contrary to French public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the commercial court registry (greffe) rejects the proposed name, the incorporator may file a written petition with the President of the commercial court (Tribunal de commerce) within fifteen days of the refusal, attaching the rejection notice and evidence of the name's lawfulness. The President will decide by way of an order (ordonnance) after hearing the applicant. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may submit a corrective name to the INPI Guichet des Entreprises. A new name clearance application starts a fresh thirty-day validity window. No administrative extension is available. An appeal from the President's order may be brought before the Court of Appeal within fifteen days of the order being served.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for a SAS engaged in online retail of jewelry, watches, and fashion. The registered office (siège social) may be domiciled with a licensed société de domiciliation under Article L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code, for a maximum initial term of two years, provided that the domiciliation contract includes physical postal collection, administrative reception, and access to professional premises during normal business hours. A mere mailbox without substantive reception services will not satisfy tax and administrative substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10% to 15% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection during the first 24 months of registration, reflecting the medium-risk AML classification of the jewelry and watch subsidiary and the French tax administration's priority on e-commerce VAT and commercial presence checks.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: French Directorate-General of Public Finance (Direction générale des finances publiques, DGFiP), acting through the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the Foreign Businesses Tax Service (Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères, SIEE) where applicable. The principal online portal is impots.gouv.fr. Corporate formation and initial enterprise identification filings are generally submitted through the Guichet unique operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with enterprise identifiers maintained through the national SIRENE system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS must be incorporated through the Guichet unique, after which the entity receives a SIREN number for the legal entity and a SIRET number for each establishment. The entity must register with the competent SIE and provide its incorporation documents, articles of association, registered-office evidence, beneficial-owner information, business activity description, bank details, and expected VAT transactions. The SIE assigns or confirms the corporate income tax and VAT accounts. The French VAT number is generally formatted as FR followed by a two-digit control key and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment must register directly with the SIEE where it makes taxable French supplies, unless the applicable reverse-charge, OSS, import-VAT, or marketplace rules eliminate the registration obligation. Non-EU businesses generally require a French fiscal representative for VAT compliance unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement or statutory exception applies. An EORI number must be obtained from French Customs for customs declarations and import or export activity. VAT registration does not replace customs, OSS, Intrastat, consumer-law, or payment-service registrations where separately applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at entity level. It may, subject to statutory eligibility conditions, elect temporarily for the partnership-style regime under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code, generally for a maximum period of five financial years; the election is not a general United States-style check-the-box election. Certain qualifying family companies may elect a partnership regime under the applicable French tax rules. France has no general entity-classification check-the-box system for SAS entities and no election that generally converts a SAS into a permanent pass-through entity. Hybrid-mismatch and anti-hybrid rules may deny deductions or impose inclusion consequences, but they are not elective classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT), integrated with the European Union VAT system. Customs duties and import VAT are administered by the French Directorate-General of Customs and Indirect Taxes (Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects, DGDDI).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business, there is no general VAT registration threshold that permits taxable supplies without VAT once the business is outside the French franchise en base regime. The principal domestic franchise threshold for commercial sales, including ordinary jewelry, watches, and fashion goods, is EUR 85,000 of annual turnover, subject to the applicable tolerance threshold and statutory year-specific adjustments. A business exceeding the relevant franchise limits becomes liable for VAT under the applicable effective-date rules. A non-established business generally has no equivalent French turnover threshold and may be required to register and account for VAT from its first taxable French transaction, subject to reverse charge, import arrangements, marketplace provisions, and the One Stop Shop (OSS). For intra-EU distance sales to consumers, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold may apply, with VAT reportable through OSS or under local registrations after the threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time VAT invoice-clearance system for all private-sector transactions. Domestic B2B electronic invoicing and transaction-data e-reporting are being introduced under the French reform timetable: all businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; large and medium-sized businesses must issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from 1 September 2026, and smaller businesses from 1 September 2027, subject to legally adopted transition rules. Invoices will generally pass through an approved private platform or the public invoicing portal, with transaction and payment data reported to the tax administration. B2C transactions, exports, intra-EU supplies, and transactions outside the French domestic B2B scope may trigger separate e-reporting obligations rather than clearance. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. French invoices must satisfy statutory content, numbering, authenticity, integrity, storage, and VAT recordkeeping requirements; there is currently no general requirement for a digital tax stamp on every invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct, commonly described commercially as export zero-rating, provided the supplier is the exporter or acts through an authorized intermediary and can prove exit from the EU. Required evidence normally includes the export declaration, MRN or equivalent customs exit confirmation, transport documentation, commercial invoice, and records linking the goods, buyer, shipment, and payment. Goods supplied for export by a qualifying intermediary may also qualify where the statutory conditions are met. Services are not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer is foreign. For B2B services, the place-of-supply rule generally places taxation at the customer’s establishment and may result in an out-of-scope supply or customer reverse charge. Specific exemptions or place-of-supply rules apply to services directly connected with exports, international transport, and certain financial or intermediary services. Jewelry, watches, and fashion goods remain subject to the ordinary VAT rules unless a specific exemption applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French or EU export customs declaration containing the applicable customs procedure and shipment data
MRN and customs office exit confirmation or equivalent electronic proof that the goods left the European Union
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, values, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR, or courier manifest
Proof linking the export declaration to the specific goods and invoice, including product descriptions, quantities, serial numbers, or shipment references where relevant
Evidence of delivery or destination outside the European Union where required by the facts or requested during audit
Accounting records and VAT returns supporting the exempt export with right to deduct

Payment and order records supporting the commercial transaction; an inward remittance certificate is not generally a French statutory export-VAT document, although bank evidence may support transaction substantiation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France does not impose a general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline of 180 days for export proceeds. Export VAT exemption may be reassessed if customs exit cannot be proven, the goods did not leave the EU, the documentation is inconsistent, the customer or intermediary conditions are not met, or the transaction is fictitious. The reassessment may include unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and applicable penalties. A 40% penalty may apply for deliberate failure or deliberate inaccuracies, and an 80% penalty may apply in cases involving fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of rights, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. Late-payment interest is generally calculated under the applicable French tax rate, commonly 0.20% per month, subject to legislative changes. Incorrect customs declarations may generate customs duties, import VAT, customs interest, administrative fines, and seizure or forfeiture consequences under the Union Customs Code and French customs law. Serious tax fraud may also result in criminal prosecution, including imprisonment and substantial fines. Refund claims may be delayed, reduced, or denied where the taxable person cannot demonstrate the underlying transactions, valid invoices, payment records, export exit, or entitlement to input-VAT deduction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank monetary framework. France has no general exchange-control authority requiring routine approval for ordinary commercial foreign-exchange transactions; applicable exchange-control powers and exceptional measures derive principally from the French Monetary and Financial Code and European Union law, with the French Treasury and Ministry for the Economy responsible for certain restrictive-measure and sanctions matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions. A French SAS may generally receive, hold, convert, and remit euros and foreign currencies, subject to bank anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, beneficial-ownership, tax, and payment-transparency controls. Dividends, interest, service fees, royalties, loan repayments, and liquidation proceeds may generally be remitted to non-residents without a general French withholding authorization or foreign-exchange approval, provided that corporate-law approvals, distributable-profit tests, transfer-pricing requirements, withholding-tax analysis, treaty documentation, accounting records, and beneficial-ownership evidence are satisfied. Cross-border transactions with related parties must be commercially justified and supported by written agreements, arm's-length pricing, transfer-pricing documentation where applicable, and evidence of actual performance. Banks may delay or reject transactions involving incomplete source-of-funds evidence, high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned parties, unusual payment chains, cash-intensive activity, inconsistent invoices, third-party settlement, or unexplained beneficial-ownership structures. Cash payments and cash-equivalent transactions are subject to French limits and reporting obligations, including restrictions applicable to payments by or to French tax residents and professional traders. Import and export payments must also remain consistent with customs declarations, VAT records, commercial invoices, transport documents, and applicable sanctions controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory requirement for an exporter to surrender export proceeds to the Banque de France, no general mandatory conversion ratio, and no general statutory deadline requiring conversion of foreign-currency export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted at the holder's discretion, subject to the bank's account terms, accounting requirements, tax reporting, customs and VAT substantiation, sanctions screening, and anti-money-laundering controls. The SAS should maintain a transaction-level reconciliation between sales invoices, customs declarations, payment confirmations, refunds, chargebacks, marketplace settlements, and VAT returns. Any exceptional reporting, blocking, licensing, or asset-freezing obligation arising from EU or French sanctions, capital controls imposed during an emergency, or a specific regulated transaction must be followed separately.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection and operational disbursements, but not a complete substitute for a French bank. EU-authorized electronic-money institutions and payment institutions may provide IBAN accounts, payment initiation, card acquiring, foreign-exchange conversion, and merchant settlement under their authorization and passporting status. An electronic-money account is not a bank deposit and generally does not provide deposit-guarantee protection; customer funds are safeguarded under the applicable authorization regime. Offshore digital EMIs without an EU authorization, French passporting basis, or acceptable correspondent arrangement should not be used for core corporate treasury. Stripe and PayPal may be used for customer collections only after merchant underwriting, with settlement to an account accepted by the provider. The SAS should retain a regulated bank account for capitalization, tax payments, payroll, supplier settlements, reserve liquidity, refunds, chargebacks, and continuity. Fintech onboarding may be restricted for jewelry, watches, luxury goods, high-value goods, cross-border sales, elevated refund rates, marketplace activity, crypto exposure, or delivery to high-risk jurisdictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance is not universally mandated by French law for opening a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available where the bank can reliably verify the legal entity, directors, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, identity documents, address, tax status, source of funds, expected activity, and control structure. The bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, certified documents, a video interview, qualified electronic identification, a French business address, or a visit to a branch. For an SAS owned or controlled by non-residents, a French-resident director is not generally required solely to incorporate the entity, but non-resident ownership and management materially increase onboarding documentation and verification requirements. The bank may refuse onboarding without giving a detailed reason, subject to applicable legal constraints.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner; ownership chain involving multiple jurisdictions or nominee arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Kbis extract or incorporation evidence; articles of association; shareholder register; complete ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and proof of address; director appointment evidence; tax-residence information; declarations of control; corporate registry extracts and legalized or apostilled documents where requested; explanation of the commercial rationale for the structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jewelry, watches, luxury goods, or other high-value merchandise classified as enhanced-risk activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; product catalogue and pricing; supplier and customer profiles; anti-counterfeit and product-authenticity procedures; customs and import documentation; insurance arrangements; logistics contracts; inventory controls; expected monthly transaction volumes; refund and chargeback policy; evidence that prohibited precious-metal, gemstone, or second-hand-dealer activities are not being conducted without required registration or compliance measures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capitalization or planned inbound shareholder funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; bank statements; audited or management accounts of the funding entity; tax returns or financial statements; board or shareholder resolutions; proof of accumulated earnings or financing; remitting-bank details; source-of-wealth explanation for individual funders; purpose code and payment narrative matching the legal documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border payment flows inconsistent with the declared French e-commerce model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-by-country flow map; supplier and customer contracts; platform and marketplace agreements; sample invoices; customs declarations; payment-service-provider statements; shipping and delivery evidence; VAT registration and filings; forecast by currency, corridor, counterparty, and payment purpose; explanation of any third-party collection or settlement arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, third-party accounts, cash, informal money-transfer channels, or unexplained payment intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury policy; segregation-of-funds controls; approved bank-account list; payment authorization matrix; prohibition of personal and unapproved third-party accounts; reconciliations; counterparty due-diligence files; documented exceptions; remediation evidence and independent review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control, high-risk-country, politically exposed person, or adverse-media exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-owner screening results; customer and supplier screening records; sanctions and export-control policy; country-risk assessment; end-use and end-customer checks; enhanced due-diligence memorandum; legal review of applicable EU and French restrictive measures; transaction-blocking and escalation procedure; documentary evidence demonstrating that no prohibited party or destination is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch among registered activity, website, payment descriptors, invoices, and actual goods sold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated corporate-purpose and activity records; website terms and conditions; merchant-account descriptors; product and brand authorization; supplier invoices; inventory ledger; marketing materials; explanation of any change in activity; timely notification to the bank and payment providers before material business-model changes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High chargeback, refund, fraud, card-not-present, or delivery-failure profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fraud-prevention rules; 3-D Secure and payment-authentication configuration; customer-verification controls; delivery tracking; signature-on-delivery procedures for high-value goods; refund-reserve model; chargeback monitoring; dispute evidence; customer-service records; stock and fulfillment controls; contingency liquidity for processor reserves.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-residency, FATCA, CRS, or beneficial-owner information incomplete or inconsistent
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax identification details; registered-office evidence; tax-residency certificates where relevant; FATCA and CRS self-certifications; entity classification; controlling-person forms; beneficial-owner declarations; consistency check against corporate registers, accounting records, and banking documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected foreign-currency activity without a documented treasury policy
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy; permitted currencies and counterparties; hedging mandate; exposure limits; segregation of dealing, confirmation, settlement, and reconciliation duties; valuation methodology; hedge-accounting position; monthly exposure reports; bank confirmations; procedures for derivatives documentation and collateral.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a regulated bank or authorized payment institution capable of identifying the remitter and beneficiary. For paid-in SAS capital, route funds to the designated capital-deposit account before incorporation or capital increase, using the exact legal name of the SAS or subscriber and the bank's prescribed capital-deposit reference. Obtain the deposit certificate and transfer the funds to the operational account only after registration and release procedures are completed. For shareholder loans or additional funding, use a written loan, contribution, or subscription agreement and transfer from an account held in the funder's own name. Payment instructions should state the precise purpose, such as 'paid-in share capital', 'shareholder loan pursuant to agreement dated [date]', or 'equity contribution', and should not describe an equity injection as trade revenue. Maintain SWIFT or SEPA payment confirmation, remitter identity, ownership evidence, board or shareholder approval, source-of-funds records, general-ledger entries, and intercompany documentation. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments and SWIFT cross-border wires for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions. No general Banque de France pre-approval or French foreign-exchange registration is required for ordinary inbound capital, but banks may apply enhanced due diligence and sanctions screening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro supplier payments and SWIFT MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 customer-credit-transfer messaging for non-SEPA payments. Payment files should contain accurate originator, beneficiary, bank, invoice, purchase-order, customs, and purpose information. For higher-value, new-counterparty, or jurisdictionally sensitive transactions, use a commercial documentary letter of credit, standby letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank-guaranteed payment where commercially appropriate. A commercial LC should specify issuing and advising banks, applicant, beneficiary, amount, currency, Incoterms, shipment dates, documents required, inspection requirements, discrepancy rules, sanctions clauses, and governing rules such as UCP 600 where selected. Reconcile every payment to the supplier invoice, purchase order, goods-receipt or transport evidence, customs declaration, and inventory record. Avoid third-party settlement unless contractually justified, approved under the bank's policy, and supported by a complete payment-chain explanation. For card and wallet collections, use Stripe or PayPal only under approved merchant terms, maintain settlement and reserve reconciliations, and do not treat processor balances as unrestricted bank liquidity. Monitor SEPA Instant, card-network, acquiring, chargeback, refund, and reserve risks separately.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts for forecast or committed receivables and payables, subject to bank credit limits, documented exposure, suitability or appropriateness controls, confirmation procedures, and a board-approved hedging policy.

Non-deliverable forwards may be used for currencies or jurisdictions where delivery is restricted or impractical, provided the counterparty is authorized, the transaction is legally permitted in the relevant jurisdiction, settlement currency and fixing source are documented, and sanctions and local-control rules are observed.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps may be used for recurring or longer-term currency funding exposures, subject to negotiated master documentation, collateral or margin terms, valuation, counterparty-credit limits, and applicable European Market Infrastructure Regulation reporting, clearing, risk-mitigation, and trade-repository requirements.

FX options, collars, and option-based structures may be used only where the SAS understands premium, strike, barrier, settlement, early-termination, and contingent-liability risks; complex or leveraged products should require enhanced board approval.

Spot foreign-exchange transactions may be used for ordinary settlement and liquidity conversion. Hedging should be linked to identifiable commercial exposure, documented at inception, reconciled to underlying invoices or forecasts, and reviewed for accounting, tax, transfer-pricing, and financial-reporting treatment. The SAS should not engage in unauthorized financial-services activity, speculative dealing unrelated to its business, or transactions with unregulated or sanctioned counterparties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder decision approving financial statements, management report and allocation of profits/losses
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records (minute book); no external regulatory filing is separately required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of financial year-end; for a calendar-year close of 31 December, no later than 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If not approved within the statutory six-month period, the SAS is exposed to judicial summons to convene a decision, civil liability of management, and potential criminal fine for omission from management/board report (up to EUR 9,000).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, income statement, notes, and management report) filed with the Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Guichet Unique operated by INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval and no later than seven months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing leads to RCS registrar injunction, court-ordered filing with daily fine (astreinte), director monetary penalties, and eventual judicial radiation from the RCS after formal notice for continued non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation income tax return (liasse fiscale - Forms 2065 and 2050 series)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) - Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year financial close, online e-filing by 15 May; paper filing by the second business day after 1 May (usually 3 May), or within three months of a non-calendar year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or omission triggers an automatic 5% penalty (10% after formal written demand) plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.2%; ex officio assessment if no return is filed within 60 days after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local economic contribution declaration (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises - Form 1447-C)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) in the municipality of the registered office or principal establishment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year businesses, e-filing by 15 May; paper return due on 3 May; final CFE payment falls due by 15 December of the assessment year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration incurs a 10% late-filing penalty plus an additional 10% if the return remains unfiled after a written warning; unpaid CFE bears monthly late-payment interest of 0.2% and a 5% base penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Updated beneficial-owner (UBO) declaration if any shareholding or control change has occurred since the previous filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS via Guichet Unique operated by INPI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in ultimate beneficial ownership details; no separate annual renewal date unless a triggering event has occurred.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update UBO information exposes the legal entity and management to administrative penalties and criminal fines up to EUR 7,500 per offending person and EUR 75,000 for the company under the French Monetary and Financial Code.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least two of the following three figures as at the previous financial year-end and for the preceding year: total balance sheet assets over EUR 4,000,000; net turnover exclusive of VAT over EUR 8,000,000; average workforce over 50. External audit can also be required by the articles of association, by court decision, or when the SAS is the parent entity of a group required to produce consolidated accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory annual accounts must be prepared in accordance with French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général - PCG) under regulation ANC 2014-03 as amended. IFRS as endorsed by the EU may be used only where French law permits optional consolidated financial statements and is not available for individual SAS statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France uses a registration-and-update model rather than a free-standing annual UBO renewal. The SAS must maintain an up-to-date internal register of beneficial owners and must file the Declaration of Beneficial Ownership (DBE) with the RCS at incorporation and within 30 days after any change. At the conclusion of each financial year, management must verify the shareholder register against transfers and record any controlling-ownership movement in the internal beneficial-owner register; if a triggering change occurred, the RCS declaration must be amended within the 30-day period, including after any share transfer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year in provincial cities; USD 1,500 - USD 3,500 in Paris for a physical registered office, mail handling, and corporate secretarial support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 15,000 for a small to mid-sized e-commerce SAS subject to statutory audit; USD 3,000 - USD 6,000 for a non-statutory limited review in the absence of mandatory audit thresholds.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax under Article 219 of the French General Tax Code, plus a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% of eligible innovation expenditure up to EUR 400,000; partial exemption for long-term capital gains on qualifying share disposals; optional French tax consolidation under Article 223 A for groups holding at least 95%
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time limit); annual offset of carryforward losses restricted to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return) with annexes 2052-SD to 2059-SD; mandatory electronic filing through impots.gouv.fr or the EDI-TDFC interchange system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; corporate income tax is paid in four quarterly instalments (15 March, 15 June, 15 September, 15 December) followed by settlement with the annual return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, the deadline is in practice the second working day after 1 May, usually 3 May

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before tax, after depreciation, provisions and legally required exclusion of income tax accounting entries
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the French entity or French permanent establishment result; foreign parent/head-office income must not be included

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box WA: Resultat fiscal avant imputation des deficits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax result after restoring disallowed expenses, applying fiscal add-backs and deductions, and reflecting transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Basis must be at arm's length; intercompany profit loads from offshore related suppliers must be documented before filing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior years, subject to the EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% annual cap
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent losses cannot be imputed to the French entity; only French taxable losses and French permanent establishment losses are eligible

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable result after loss carryforward and before tax credits; constitutes the base for corporate income tax at 25% or 15%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute taxable profit solely from French-source e-commerce activity; non-resident shareholders cannot use the entity's taxable loss to calculate their own tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits and reductions including Research Tax Credit and Innovation Tax Credit, reported after gross tax is calculated
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident company with a French permanent establishment may credit CIR/CII only for work effectively performed in France; expenses must be substantiated

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing within 30 days after deadline: 10% surcharge on tax due; after 30 days or formal notice: 40%; failure to file after formal notice: 100%; late-payment interest 0.20% per month; omitted or false information may attract an additional 5% penalty and 80% penalty for fraudulent concealment

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Article 119 bis 2 of the French General Tax Code; 75% for distributions to non-cooperative States; 0% if the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies to a qualifying EU/EEA parent holding at least 5% for two years
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must obtain a certificate of tax residence (Form 5000/5001) from the foreign tax authority and submit it to the French withholding agent or tax administration before distribution; if the treaty rate is applied after withholding, the shareholder files a refund claim within the statutory period, generally before the end of the second year following tax payment, attaching the TRC, dividend vouchers, and evidence of beneficial ownership
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents: domestic statutory withholding 33.33%; treaty rates usually range from 0% to 10%. Interest paid to non-residents: generally no domestic withholding on arm's-length negotiated loans not made to non-cooperative jurisdictions, with treaty rates typically 0% to 10%; payments to non-cooperative States may be taxed at 75%

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 consolidated gross turnover or gross total assets of a qualifying group with at least 50% direct or indirect French/foreign cross-border ownership links and with the French entity in the scope; below the threshold the French entity must still retain sufficient transfer pricing evidence to demonstrate arm's-length pricing
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply offshore Economic Substance Regulations as in OFC regimes; however, the substance-over-form principle, abuse of law under Article L.64 of the French Tax Procedures Book, and ATAD anti-abuse rules require a French SAS to carry on genuine economic activity in France, including French employees, real inventory, actual management decisions, local bank accounts, and substantive commercial risk control

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting online jewelry/timepiece sales revenue, deleting Stripe/PayPal transaction records, issuing fake supplier invoices, or routing e-commerce profits through non-tax-resident related shell companies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties of 40% to 80% of evaded tax, 0.20% monthly interest, criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 or double the tax evaded, imprisonment up to five years, confiscation of assets and proceeds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: SAS President and directors may be held personally liable under Article L.267 of the French Tax Procedures Book for corporate tax debts where serious misconduct and bad faith are shown; courts may impose management bans, travel restrictions, and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS as a letterbox entity with no real French decision-making, employees, inventory or operational substance, while claiming French tax residence or treaty benefits for foreign-owned e-commerce activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment under the abuse-of-law procedure with an 80% penalty in case of abuse; denial of treaty benefits; recharacterization of the French structure as a permanent establishment of the foreign parent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly maintain a fictitious entity may be jointly and severally liable for reassessed tax, interest and penalties; judicial management disqualification and sequestration of personal assets are possible

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border purchases of jewelry, watches, brand fees, or management fees from related parties without arm's-length pricing, and failure to produce contemporaneous Master File/Local File documentation within 30 days of formal request
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment by the French tax administration; penalty of 5% of reassessed profits under Article 1735 ter of the French General Tax Code, increased to 10% in abuse cases; additional fixed penalties for documents not produced after formal notice; risk of economic double taxation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false certificates, approve circular transactions, or fail to prevent gross negligence may be ordered to pay the resulting corporate liabilities, with personal bankruptcy measures if the company is insolvent

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash payments above the legal French ceilings (EUR 1,000 for resident consumers; EUR 15,000 for non-resident tourists) in luxury jewelry sales, failing to report suspicious transactions to Tracfin, or ignoring enhanced due diligence for high-risk corporate buyers
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to EUR 500,000, confiscation of goods, administrative sanctions by Tracfin/AMF/customs authorities, VAT and customs penalties up to 80%, and possible termination of payment processing services by Stripe or PayPal
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or officers who personally direct or tolerate AML/cash-payment violations incur individual criminal liability, imprisonment up to five years, civil restitution, and, where corporate assets are dissipated, attachment of personal assets
